paper: Minimum-word reconstruction of PG(2,13) from a binary conic code

claims.statement: The binary passant incidence code has length 78 and dimension 36.
current_modes: Lean-checked recovery and expansion maps identifying the 42-column basis with the semantic incidence-map range
claims.lean_boundary: closed: the paper-owned aggregate proves semantic incidence-map rank 42 and code dimension 36

current_modes: human global line-incidence and passant-pair moment
four line-stabilizer and thirty-three point-stabilizer exact leaves
old syndrome and clique programs retained only as independent cross-checks
Lean structural implication packets with declaration-local finite leaves
claims.lean_boundary: the shared semantic transport reaches the 42-vertex tangent graph and arbitrary weight-ten support; the theta positivity data and the two stabilizer tables are named paper-owned exact leaves, while the quadratic-form clique implication and moment algebra are kernel checked

claims.statement: There are 364 minimum words in four PGL(2,13)-orbits of size 91.
current_modes: Lean native exhaustion of the four fixed-point pencil-profile domains
Lean identification of their 56 solutions with four disjoint 14-support orbit slices
Lean transitivity of the order-28 fixed-point stabilizer on each 14-support slice
Lean execution of four projective kernel orbits of size 91
Lean rank-36 check for each orbit
claims.lean_boundary: the fixed-point exhaustion is closed by PassantCodeQ13.Gates.Main.fixedPointWeightTwelveExhaustion; transport to all 364 supports uses the human projective-transitivity and double-count argument

claims.statement: Each minimum-word orbit spans the 36-dimensional code.
current_modes: Lean native relation squaring and orbit Gram identities
Lean theorem that each orbit row space equals the rho-zero kernel
claims.lean_boundary: the compact operator-field and Gram-to-spanning implication are kernel checked relative to the relation and Gram leaves; polarity identifies A0 with the incidence matrix up to row order

claims.statement: The weighted 2-section reconstructs the elliptic scheme, the 78 passant incidence rows, and the code; reconstruction arity is exactly two.
current_modes: exact pair-concurrence table and common-concurrence-7 split
exact pair-parity power table and rank
Lean pair-derived coherent split and unary-constancy interface
claims.lean_boundary: the theorem-facing row family is concurrence-8 neighborhood recovery, not the superseded seven-clique/triple filter; concrete pair-table and rank inputs remain named exact leaves

claims.statement: The coordinate-permutation automorphism group of the minimum-support system is PGL(2,13).
current_modes: Lean symbolic transport identifying all polar-relation automorphisms with the 2184 normalized symmetric-square maps
claims.lean_boundary: the four-anchor classification is closed for the six-valued polar-relation scheme; transport from support automorphisms now uses weighted-pair equivariance rather than triple concurrence

claims.statement: The weighted 2-section reconstructs all 183 points and lines of PG(2,13), its conic, and its polarity.
current_modes: human adjoint sl2 and trace-polarity proof
claims.lean_boundary: the group-theoretic incidence rules and recovery implication are theorem-shaped; the concrete enumeration of Sylow subgroups, involutions, and all polarity incidences remains a named paper-owned exact leaf

claims.statement: The four minimum families are one octahedral and three chord-indexed punctured-conic families.
current_modes: human toric conic-pencil construction and discriminant parity proof
exact orbit, stabilizer, syndrome, and Gram replay
Lean toric parity packet and octahedral finite interface
claims.lean_boundary: the three toric support constructions and parity implication are semantic theorems; the standard octahedral six-suborbit classification remains a named finite leaf

claims.statement: The binary code is a 12-dimensional module over the operator field F8, with A9, A10, A12 the Frobenius-conjugate scalars.
claims.lean_boundary: only the compact operator-field theorem needed for spanning is retained; absolute irreducibility, Schur-field completeness, symplectic refinement, and cuspidal identification are deliberately outside the paper
